# Desk x-ray (2026-10-13)

Owner's request: "a full xray of our system, investigated, tested … ensure that each form or point of information actually
makes sense, when entered/researched/submitted - does something and works … the worst thing we can do is add more
functionality that doesn't actually make sense."

## How it was checked
- **Inventory.** All 127 API endpoints, all 22 cockpit pages, all 31 components, and every server action in `cockpit/app/actions.ts` (each form's fields compared with what its endpoint reads).
- **Reading.** Every page and form, read as a user, with each input traced to what it writes and to who reads that later.
- **Running.** Two end-to-end walks on a scratch database, with fake model and fake Exa, at no cost. They do what the cockpit does and record whether each entry reaches the places that should use it. The scripts are `core/tests/xray_journey.py` and `xray_journey2.py` (they report, they don't fail): 21 checks, 13 failed.
- **Live data.** The dev database: what is stored, what is spent, which tasks failed and why.
- **The full test suite** passes (454 tests; one calls test failed once and passed on re-run), so each feature works on its own. Almost every finding below is **between** features.

## A. Broken: it says it worked, but it did not (fix without a decision)

| # | Where | What happens | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| A1 | Sourcing tab → Titles and countries | Typing "Italy" (not "IT") saves "a new version of the plan", but the country is silently dropped. If every country is typed as a name, the role then searches **with no country limit**. | walk 1: sent `ITALY, DE` → stored `["DE"]` |
| A2 | Messages tab → "I sent it myself" / "They replied" | The message is marked sent/replied and the pair becomes "contacted", but the contact track on the Sourcing tab is not filled: no channel, no date, no follow-up line. **The LinkedIn email reader never watches that person.** "They replied" does not move the card to Replied. | walk 1: track stayed `{stage: to_contact}`; reader watched `[]` |
| A3 | Results and spend | "They replied: interested" (one click on the card) is not counted as Interested. Only a recorded permission, or the Screened stage, counts. | walk 2: contacted 1, replied 1, **interested 0** |
| A4 | Company page | 43 companies' research failed today because the shared research budget is used up. Their page says "Not researched yet. Research runs on its own…", which is untrue, and nothing says the budget is reached. | live: 43 failed `BudgetExceeded`, `research_status` empty |
| A5 | Costs page | The shared company-research budget ($10, **used up: $10.21**) is shown only as a spend figure, with no limit and no warning. Four kinds of spend show their code names (`sourcing_company_profile`, `company_domains`, `sourcing_talent_dna`, `read_transcript`). | live cost ledger |
| A6 | Strategy refusal message | "Exa could not confirm X by its website or LinkedIn page: research it first, or add …". For a company with no website or LinkedIn on record, Exa is **never asked**. And the company page has no field to add a website. My earlier advice to "add its website on its company page" was impossible. | `company_profiles.by_name` returns before searching |
| A7 | Many buttons | Approve, Reject, Save (strength), Brief answers, tags, call review apply, mailbox sync, Same company? …: a refusal from the API (404/409/422) is swallowed by `idempotent()`. When one is refused for a real reason, **nothing happens on screen**. | `actions.ts` `idempotent()`; walk 1: an invalid strength is refused (422), the cockpit would show nothing |
| A8 | Several actions | Band override ("Set band"), "They have X", Put on job, member role and remove: no error handling, so a refusal shows the crash page instead of a message. | `actions.ts` |
| A9 | Hiring profile → Mobility panel | The intake's city and "relocation welcome" (Milan) are stored but not shown. The panel says only "Italy". | `jobs/[id]/page.tsx` `facetValue` |

## B. Disconnected: two features that should agree, but don't (the fix needs one rule from you)

| # | What | Today | What it should be (proposal) |
|---|---|---|---|
| B1 | **"Countries" exists three times on one role** | (1) the Countries tab: who is archived as outside coverage; (2) the Hiring profile "must live in": who sourcing suggests; (3) the Sourcing plan's countries: where it searches. The Countries tab never reaches sourcing (walk 1: opened Spain → plan and suggestions unchanged). The plan only ever **adds** countries from the hiring profile: "must live in Italy" left Germany in the plan (walk 2: `["DE","IT"]`). | **One place: the hiring profile's "must live in"**. The Sourcing plan shows it (editable there, written back to the hiring profile). The Countries tab becomes only "also accept people living in …" for coverage, or merges into the same field. |
| B2 | **Contact is recorded in four places, which don't know each other** | The Sourcing card ("Contacted by …"), the Messages tab ("I sent it myself"), the person-on-job page's stage control ("contacted"), and "Log a call … we reached out … about job X". Only the first fills the track; the stage control gives no follow-up (walk 1); a logged outgoing call about the job **does not count as contact at all** (walk 1: pair stayed `new`). | **One "contacted" record**, whichever door is used: each of the four writes the same track (channel, date, follow-up due), so the card, the follow-up reminder, the LinkedIn reader, freshness and the results all agree. |
| B3 | **"Not from" companies are ignored by sourcing** | A hiring-profile "not from Orbital Testworks" keeps the company off the target list, but people who work there now are still suggested (walk 2: Ada, at Orbital Testworks, suggested). "No candidates from big consultancies" is not used by sourcing at all. | Treat "not from" as off-limits **for that role**: its current people are refused like an off-limits company. Background "anti" kinds (consultancy, agency…) leave those companies out of the peer list. |
| B4 | **Two ways to search the pool, two ways to find peer companies** | "Search the desk only, by hand" (Slice 2 campaigns) repeats what every sourcing run already does first (pool before web). Its "thin" pill uses its own target of 5, not the plan's target (walk 2: 5 vs 10). "Find peer companies on the web" repeats the strategy's peer search with an older query. | **Remove both**: the strategy and the run do this, with one target. |
| B5 | **Permission is recorded, but nothing uses it** | Permission is shown on the person page and counted in the results. A person can be marked **Submitted** with no permission (walk 1: 200 OK). | Your call (you asked to keep compliance minimal): either a warning ("no permission recorded for this role") on Submitted, or leave it. A double submission to a client is the business risk. |
| B6 | **A role cannot be closed or deleted** | Jobs have the states open, on hold, filled and cancelled, but nothing can change them, so every role stays open and keeps its sourcing and counts. | Close (filled / cancelled / on hold: sourcing stops, lists hide it, history kept) and Delete (a role added by mistake, with confirmation). (You asked for this.) |
| B7 | **"To review" means two things on one role** | The role header's "N to review" and the Jobs list's "To review" are inbox questions. The Sourcing tab's "To review" is new suggestions. | Rename the inbox one "questions"; keep "To review" for suggestions. |
| B8 | **Company knowledge is in two halves** | The company page shows the Grok research facts. The Exa profile (staff, markets, team countries, funding) that the strategy uses is shown only on the Sourcing tab. A company's website or LinkedIn cannot be typed anywhere. | The company page shows both, with a field for the website or LinkedIn page. With it, Exa can confirm the company and build the talent DNA (it is how BUONAVENTURA would get one). |

## C. A cost decision (works as built, but costs more than its budget)

- **Every company on every CV gets Grok research (about $0.09 each).** This morning, re-checking coverage for everyone queued 88 at once (about $8), against a shared research budget of $10, which is now used up. This month: shared research $10.21 (company research is $9.28 of all research ever spent), the desk's own model work $1.02, sourcing $0.64.
- The 1b design already has a cheaper level: the **Exa profile** (about $0.001–0.015) for breadth, with Grok kept for depth.
- **Proposal:** Exa profile by default for companies on CVs. Grok only for hiring companies, named targets and "Research now". Optionally raise the shared budget while deciding.

## What was not walked end to end
Import, mailbox connection (no mailbox yet), members and sign-in, the Brief, calls, merge and erasure were read and are covered by their own tests (all pass), but were not exercised across features in the walks above.

## Endpoints nothing in the cockpit uses
- **For developers only (fine):** `GET/POST /v1/documents…`, `/v1/runs/{id}`, `/v1/jobs/{id}/people`, `/v1/candidates/{id}/claims`, `/v1/subjects/…/erase/verify`, `GET /v1/call-reviews/{id}`.
- **Dead:** `POST /v1/campaigns/{id}/stop` (a campaign finishes before it could be stopped), `POST /v1/companies/{id}/merge` (companies merge through the "Same company?" card).
- **Missing in the cockpit:** `POST /v1/auth/two-step/disable` (owners must keep two-step, so this is fine).
